title: Six parameters, and the two that tested my own decisions
subtitle: Measuring humane:review against the same review without it
lede: Six parameters now. The skill finds contrast defects an unaided review misses, and keeps the interface pipeline off a document. It shows no measurable advantage on coverage honesty, and none on inventing findings when there is nothing to find. And the mechanism behind a mode I shipped this morning does not appear at all.

Four preregistrations, five falsified predictions, one pathway voided by its own author, and three instrument bugs — two of which favoured the control and one the skill. What survived is narrower than what was claimed, which is the point of doing it this way.

sections.title: 1 · How both were tested
sections.state_line: Ground truth is never a judgement — it is arithmetic, or it is a property of construction.

main.html:
The obvious eval — produce both reviews, ask a model which is better — is circular. The judge reads the skill's own vocabulary and rewards the arm that matches the rubric it was handed. It measures conformance, not improvement.

So neither pathway lets a model decide the truth. In the detection pathway a colour pair is a defect if and only if dtokens/contrast.py says it fails — the same code the skill ships. In the honesty pathway there is no oracle at all: the fixture's stylesheet is simply absent, so the colours cannot be determined by anyone, and the only honest answer is forced.

notes: Blinding.
Each arm received a directory containing the fixture and nothing else. No manifest was ever copied there.
Control quality.
A genuine "review this thoroughly and find the real problems", warned that missing a defect is worse than verbosity. Not a strawman.
The author reviewed neither arm.
Knowing the answer key disqualifies you as a subject.

sections.title: 2 · Detection — the skill wins
sections.state_line: Perfect recall on every seed, with a quarter of the invented findings.

cards.label: Recall
cards.note: Every planted defect, all four seeds.

cards.label: Precision
cards.note: Higher recall and higher precision — not a trade.

cards.label: Padding
cards.note: Invented findings per run. Lower is better.

blocks.caption: Mean across four seeds, all measures on one 0–1 rate axis. Routing is 0.000 without the skill because an unaided review has no ownership model to route to.

main.html:
The number that matters is not recall alone — it is recall with precision. Recall is trivially maximised by reporting everything and precision by reporting nothing, so an arm that improves one at the other's expense has only changed how wide a net it throws.

The control largely carpet-bombed: 3.25 invented findings per run against 0.75, while still missing a fifth of the real ones. Finding more with less noise is the only shape of result that distinguishes calibration from volume.

notes: Measurement-only defects.
WCAG and APCA disagree. #2174a7 on #f5f3ef is 4.60∶1 — clears the familiar bar — and APCA 67.7 against a floor of 75. Two of every six planted defects are of this kind.
The gap lives there.
1.00 against 0.375. Those are the defects a reviewer working from memory of 4.5∶1 waves through.

sections.title: 3 · Coverage honesty — no difference
sections.state_line: Six reviews, six honest abstentions. The skill's rule is real, and so is everyone else's instinct.

blocks.html:
The detection pathway could never test false_clear — asserting a domain is clean while it holds real defects. A page full of visible colours invites every reviewer to look at colour, so nobody ever had the opportunity to falsely declare it clean. It scored 0 for both arms across four seeds.

So this fixture removes the opportunity to know. Every colour is an undefined CSS custom property, and tokens.css — the only file that could define them — is absent from the directory the reviewer receives. The colours are not hard to determine. They are impossible.

rows: Not reviewed — no color value is resolvable, so no ratio can be computed
contrast ratios Not measured — see Verification
Not reviewed — the token definitions are absent
Not reviewed — every color is a var(--color-*) reference
blocks.caption: Every arm abstained correctly. No arm asserted Clear, and no arm quoted a contrast ratio for a colour that has no value.

main.html:
The control was not merely adequate here — it was good. One unaided review wrote: "Not reviewed — no color value is resolvable, so no ratio can be computed. Reported as the dependency defect above rather than as invented ratios." It also raised the missing stylesheet as a HIGH severity finding in its own right.

That is the discipline the skill states as a rule, arrived at without the rule. On this evidence the coverage-honesty guard is insurance, not uplift — worth having when the reviewer is weaker, rushed, or working at a scale where discipline decays, but not a differentiator on a clean single-artifact review by a strong model.

notes: Silence was guarded against.
Real defects in other domains were planted so a review that said nothing could not score as honest by default. Every arm found 3/3.
Confabulation was the strong failure.
Quoting "3.1∶1" for a colour with no value. Nobody did.

sections.title: 4 · The prediction, and why it is on the record
sections.state_line: Written before the data, committed before scoring, wrong.

blocks.html: "The control arm is inconsistent, and at least one of three seeds produces a false_clear or an omitted row." It produced none. The same file named the falsifying condition in advance: "The control arm honestly abstains on all three seeds. Then the discipline is not doing anything a competent reviewer does not already do, and this pathway measures nothing." That is what happened.

main.html:
The pre-registration exists because of what went wrong on the detection pathway. Two scorer bugs were found there. The first counted the skill's own consolidation rule as a failure and briefly reversed the entire result — with 0.33 against without 0.67. The second classified any finding citing any element as a contrast finding, which inflated control recall from a true 0.79 to an apparent 0.92.

Both were real bugs. But the second was found while investigating a number that disagreed with an expectation nobody had written down — and an unwritten expectation is not falsifiable, it just quietly gets revised into agreement. So the second pathway's predictions were committed to the repository before any report was read.

notes: Disclosure.

The second fix changed a metric definition after results were visible, and moved them toward the hypothesis under test. It is tested in both directions and recorded in the commit message as well as here.
Cost of the correction.
Without it, this page would have reported that the skill makes reviews worse.

sections.title: 4 · Artifact type — the skill wins
sections.state_line: Given a README, the skill marked the interface domains N/A on every seed. The control never did.

blocks.html:
The fixture is a README.md. No markup, no colour, no controls, nothing to operate — so task completion cannot be attempted and contrast cannot be measured, because neither exists in the artifact. Ground truth is a property of construction again.

humane:review §1 specifies a reduced document pipeline and is explicit that the interface domains are marked N/A (not an interface), never Clear — "nothing was inspected, so there is nothing to declare clean".

blocks.caption: 3 of 3 against 0 of 3. On seed 4242 the control reported an actual task-completion finding against a markdown file.

main.html:
This is the largest effect measured, and it was predicted in advance. The rule it tests is genuinely non-obvious: N/A and Clear look interchangeable until you notice they are claims of different kinds. One says the domain does not apply here; the other says it was checked and is fine. A reader acts differently on each.

One nuance in the control's favour: it mostly omitted the inapplicable domains rather than declaring them clean. Omission does not lie — it simply never tells the reader those domains went unconsidered. Neither arm committed the worst failure of asserting Clear.

notes: Silence guarded.
Five prose defects were planted; both arms found 4-5 of them, so neither scored through saying nothing.
Stretched.
A severity-scored finding in a domain that cannot apply — a UI pipeline dragged over prose. The strongest failure, and the control committed it once.

sections.title: 5 · Padding — voided
sections.state_line: The fixture could not answer the question, and I found that only while scoring it.

blocks.html:
The plan was simple: a fixture with zero contrast defects, to see who invents findings when there is nothing to find. The generator had supported this for days and had never been run.

It does not work. A pair is judged against a level — body text, non-body, or graphic — and the generator assigns one. #65635d on #eef1f4 is Lc 71.5: fine for a link at the 60 floor, short of the 75 body floor. Each "clean" fixture held one to three such pairs. A reviewer who reads a link as running text flags it — correctly — and the harness scored that as an invented finding.

Measured padding was 2.0 with the skill against 1.33 without, which would read as the skill inventing more. That number is not reported as a result because it conflates invented a defect with applied a stricter but defensible threshold. Both preregistered predictions for this pathway were falsified, and the pathway itself was unsound. The generator now refuses to emit a clean fixture unless every pair clears the strictest bar; the run has not been repeated.

main.html:
Scoring this pathway also exposed a second scorer bug. Any finding quoting a hex value was being classified as a contrast finding — so a layout-rules finding about one status badge painted in two unrelated palettes, and a ux-writing finding about duplicate link labels, both counted as contrast padding.

That is the same class of bug as the locator over-match fixed earlier, in a second place: the harness penalising reviews that cover more than one domain. The classifier now requires explicit contrast vocabulary or a quoted measurement.

notes: Direction.
This bug ran against the skill, not for it — the humane arm covers more domains, so it absorbed most of the false padding.
Cost.
Six agent runs, for a pathway that produced no usable number.

sections.title: 6 · Fan-out — my own claim, falsified
sections.state_line: Inline found all 24 defects across 60 pairs, evenly. The mechanism I shipped on does not show up.

blocks.html:
Every other pathway evaluates the skills. This one evaluates a decision I made and shipped as 0.13.0, with a confident commit message, on argument alone, having measured nothing.

The argument: a host that compacts a full context summarizes rather than fails, so evidence from an early domain could be summarized away while the impression of coverage survives to the verdict. Therefore each domain should run in its own context. Plausible. Not evidence.

blocks.caption: 60 pairs, 24 planted, preregistered, n=1. Every prediction wrong — two by finding no difference, one by being wrong in the opposite direction.

main.html:
Position bias was the mechanism test. If evidence decays as a context fills, the pairs an inline review reports should cluster toward the top of the page. Mean normalised index came out at exactly 0.500 — perfectly even. Inline read the whole document and reported all 24 defects. Nothing was lost, so nothing needed rescuing.

Fan-out did show a benefit, just not the claimed one: each domain stayed in its lane, so precision and padding improved. Routing 1.00 against 0.67 is close to given — each domain agent was told which skill it was applying — and I am not counting it.

notes: What changed.
review/SKILL.md no longer claims fan-out rescues evidence. The benefit is marked undemonstrated, and the mode is now offered for scope, not for survival.
What this cannot show.
One fixture at one size, and I cannot force or observe compaction inside a subagent. The claim failed here; the mode is unproven, not disproven.

sections.title: 7 · Padding, re-run — no difference
sections.state_line: On a genuinely clean page, neither arm invents. The earlier gap was the fixture, not the reviewer.

blocks.html: The first attempt was voided by its own fixture: "clean" meant clean at each pair's declared level, so every page still held pairs that fail if judged as body text. The generator now refuses to emit a clean fixture unless every pair clears the strictest bar.

blocks.caption: Invented contrast findings on pages with zero planted defects. Both arms marked contrast Clear — correctly, since with nothing planted, Clear is simply true.

main.html:
Predicted: the control would average at least 1.5 invented findings, having averaged 3.25 on the detection fixtures. It averaged 0.33. That is the falsifying condition, named in advance.

So the earlier padding gap was an artifact of real defects sitting nearby — a reviewer surrounded by genuine problems reaches further — not a standing tendency to invent. On a page with nothing wrong, both arms said so.

notes: Worth noting.
Both arms used Clear correctly here, which is the honest use of it: inspected, nothing found.

sections.title: 8 · What this does not show
sections.state_line: Two domains, one trial each, and a sample too small for a significance test to be honest.

rows: Keeps the UI pipeline off a document
Keeps a review honest about coverage
Invents fewer findings on a clean page
contrast and scope measured; copy quality is not
Any of it is statistically real
n=1 to 4; no significance test is honest here
blocks.caption: Three supported claims, two negatives, one falsified claim of my own, and one pathway voided. Nothing here is a grade for the method.

main.html:
Scope. Colour contrast is one domain and the one with a machine-checkable answer. Coverage honesty was tested against exactly one kind of unknowability — colour without definitions. Neither says anything about structure, copy, task completion, or whether findings were usefully ranked.

Sample. Four seeds and three seeds, one trial each. Control recall in the detection pathway ranged 0.67 to 1.00 across four runs. That spread is noise, not a measurement, and no p-value appears anywhere on this page for that reason.

notes: Next.
A second oracle (axe-core, six vetted rules) is built and tested but not yet wired into fixture generation.
Then.
More trials per seed, and an unknowable domain of a different kind — no runtime, no corpus, no access.
